name: npm-badges

schema.description: An object hash containing an `items` array and optionally a `config` object

list.description: Array of badges. Use "---" to denote a separation.

saucelabsUsername.description: The username of the SauceLabs account

saucelabsAuthToken.description:
SauceLabs auth token, should probably not be used.
Use `SAUCELABS_AUTH_TOKEN` env var instead.

travisTLD.description: The TLD to use for Travis CI. Use "com" if you have moved to travis-ci.com

codeshipProjectUUID.description: The UUID for the project, available in the General tab of your project setting.

codeshipProjectID.description: The ID for the project, available in the URL for the codeship project.

githubSlug.description: The Github slug of the project (e.g., SchemaStore/schemastore)

githubWorkflow.description: The name or location of the workflow file to show the badge for.

githubBranch.description: The branch to constrain the badge to.

githubEvent.description: The event to constrain the badge to.

nodeicoQueryString.description:
Either a query string as a string, or an object containing the options.

See https://nodei.co for details

sixtydevstipsURL.description: The URL to the 60devs donate page.

patreonUsername.description: The Patreon username to donate to.

patreonURL.description: The URL to the Patreon donate page.

opencollectiveUsername.description: The Open Collective username to donate to.

opencollectiveURL.description: The URL to the Open Collective donate page.

twitterUsername.description: The twitter username to tweet at

schema.title: Configuration for the NPM package badges.

description:
The project is published under the npm package **awesome-package**, and its source lives at GitHub under the slug myorg/awesome-package. The continuous‑integration workflow is defined in the file ci.yml, runs on the main branch for push events, and the Travis CI service is accessed via the com domain. In the README we display a series of badges in the following order: an npmversion badge, an npmdownloads badge, a visual separator, then badges for travisci, githubworkflow (and the specific workflow file ci.yml), and finally codeclimate. The nodeico badge is set to a compact layout, includes download statistics, shows data for the past 12 months, and renders at a height of 2.  

Support for the package can be shown through several channels: Patreon (user awesomecreator), Open Collective (community awesome-collective), PayPal (https://paypal.me/awesomecreator), Bitcoin (https://example.com/bitcoin), and a wishlist (https://example.com/wishlist). More information is available on the project homepage at https://awesome-package.org, and you can follow updates on Twitter @awesome_pkg or on GitHub via the user awesomecreator.
